subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@brightretail.com>, Priya Desai <p.desai@brightretail.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and so Dev/Rishi can pick up the technical/next-step items.

Key pain points you mentioned:
- Significant latency spikes during peak checkout personalization traffic (tail latency impacting user experience)
- High per-unit cost on embedding-based recommendations; want to reduce token count and inference cost
- Need deterministic reranking for A/B test comparisons and explainability for compliance

Goals
- Reduce median & tail latency for real-time personalization to < 150ms for 90% of requests
- Cut embedding/retrieval cost by ~30% while keeping top-K recall stable
- Have structured outputs and function-calling to integrate scoring directly into our existing microservices pipeline

Where Redwood fits (from the call)
- SDK + streaming: low-latency streaming to reduce perceived response time for user-facing flows
- Function calling / structured outputs: return a typed JSON payload (item_id, score, reason_code) that maps cleanly to your scoring service
- Embeddings & reranking: option to compute dense embeddings via our optimized runtime, plus an on-the-fly rerank step (cheap reranker + top-K re-score)
- Quantization and batching recommendations to hit your latency/cost targets; Dev and I sketched a 3-tier model fallback (high-perf -> quantized -> cached)

Open technical items / next steps
1) Technical deep-dive (30–45m) with your infra/ML team — demo of streaming + function-calls + embedding-rerank pipeline. Dev suggested Wed 3/4 or Thu 3/5.
2) Share mutual action plan and architecture diagram (attached). Please confirm people to include on the deep-dive.
3) Provide your expected QPS, median/tail latencies, and a sample inference request payload for accurate demo tuning.
4) Pricing/commitment: Rishi will provide a rough cost model and Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs after the technical call.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.xlsx, redwood-architecture-diagram.pdf

Thanks — I’ll follow up to lock the technical call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142
From: Samir Shah <samir@brightretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priya Desai <p.desai@brightretail.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Priority order: (1) tail latency, (2) deterministic reranking for experiments, (3) cost reduction — we want the demo to focus first on streaming + caching strategies that improve tail latency.
- For the technical call, our ML infra lead (Priya) and one of our SREs (mark.sullivan@brightretail.com) should join. Priya and I are available Wed 3/4 11:00–12:00 PT or Thu 3/5 14:00–15:00 PT.
- Can you also share your SOC 2 report and a sample SLA for Dedicated capacity? Procurement will need those ahead of any committed deal.

On the sample payload and QPS: we’ll send a small anonymized sample dataset and expected peak QPS (roughly 500 RPS for personalization during flash sale).

Thanks — looking forward to the demo.

Samir — perfect, thanks for the priority order and availability. I booked Wed 3/4 11:00–11:45 PT for the technical deep-dive and invited Priya and your SRE (marked attendees in the calendar invite). Dev — please prepare:
- Short demo (15m) showing streaming SDK latency vs non-streaming baseline
- Function-calling example returning structured score payload -> show integration with a small mock HTTP endpoint
- Embedding + rerank flow: quick demo of compute cost vs accuracy tradeoffs and how our caching layer can cut costs

Rishi — can you pull together a 1-page cost model (Hosted vs Dedicated) and a sample SLA/SOC2 pointer we can send to procurement before the call?

Samir / Priya — I attached the mutual action plan and architecture diagram again. If procurement needs a copy of SOC 2 now, Rishi will share the link and the Dedicated SLA.

Thanks — speak soon.

Best,
Marissa
